descriptions.default: A tall goddess with a feather on her head stands holding an ankh and a long staff. Davis has the deceased introduced into the hall by Truth.
A tall post carries the balance, with a plumb line hanging beside it.
The long beam of the balance, a hook at each end.
A plumb line hangs from the beam of the balance, a small weight at its end.
A pan hangs from the beam on cords. The heart lies in it.
A pan hangs from the beam on cords. The image of Truth sits in it.
A baboon sits on a flat perch at the top of the balance post.
The heart is drawn as a jar with two handles, and lies in the right pan. Davis has it weighed against the image of Truth.
A small seated figure with a feather on her head sits in the left pan: the image of Truth that the heart must weigh the same as.
A figure with a falcon's head and a long wig stands by the post of the balance with one arm raised toward it, an ankh in the other hand. Davis has Horus and Anubis weigh the heart.
A god with a jackal's head stands at the left pan, one arm stretched toward it and an ankh in the other hand. Davis has him announce that the heart weighs the same as Truth.
A small figure in a long kilt stands with one arm raised toward the pan beside him and the other held out.
Two figures in long wigs and banded garments sit side by side with their knees drawn up. Davis has two genii of destiny, Shai and Ranen, sit above the beast.
A lion's head is drawn on a long low base, a hieroglyph beside the two seated figures.
An altar loaded with offerings is topped with a bundle of lotus, and stands on a tall slender stem; a tall lotus bud rises on either side of its foot. Davis has the four funerary genii above it.
Four mummiform figures stand in a row above the altar, with the head of a man, of an ape, of a jackal and of a falcon. Davis has the four funerary genii here.
A god with an ibis's head holds a pen to a palette. Davis has Thoth, lord of the divine words, register the sentence.
A tiny figure squats on top of a shepherd's crook.
A fantastic beast with gaping jaws sits on a pedestal in the shape of a pylon, its top ribbed, watching the balance. Davis calls her the one who destroys the foes by devouring them.
The tall frame of Osiris's shrine stands on a low base, a ribbed cornice over its top.
A long dais under the throne, its side decorated with a row of ankh signs above a low flight of steps.
A tall pole rises from a base, a long spotted cloth hanging from it.
Osiris sits enthroned in the atef crown, the crook and flail held across his breast. The scene is his.
A long low ledge runs along the foot of the row of judges.
A figure in a long wig kneels with both arms raised before an offering stand.
A slender stand with a flared foot carries a round object under a cone-shaped cap.

descriptions.default: A long ledge runs under the row of cobras and signs along the top of the hall.

Twelve groups of three signs ornament the cornice: a rearing cobra, an arch with a tie round its stem, and a tall striped shape curled at the top. The groups on the left and on the right mirror each other. Davis describes them as groups formed with the hieroglyphs of truth and of fire and an uraeus.
A baboon in a long wig kneels at the right-hand end of the cornice and poises a pair of scales. Davis has one at each end of the row.
A god kneels with his arms stretched out above two eyes, each in an oval. Davis has Tmu here between the sixth and seventh groups of signs.
A baboon in a long wig kneels at the left-hand end of the cornice and poises a pair of scales. Davis has one at each end of the row.
A column of hieroglyphs runs down the page between the deceased and Ma'at, its outline broken where the drawing is damaged.

descriptions.default: A row of short columns of hieroglyphs hangs from the rule above Ma'at, and a long column runs down beside the deceased.
Three columns of hieroglyphs stand before the face of Osiris, inside his shrine.
Two columns of hieroglyphs stand beside the altar of offerings.
Two short columns of hieroglyphs stand above the two seated figures.
Three columns of hieroglyphs stand above Thoth's head and his writing.
Three columns of hieroglyphs stand above the beam of the balance, to one side of the baboon.
A bird sign and a tall stroke stand beside the raised hand of the falcon-headed attendant.
A short group of hieroglyphs, ending in a round sign over a bar, is drawn under the two seated figures.
